120	of the Infinite One, blessed be He, since He has no body nor likeness of a body, and no thought can grasp Him at all, but this is
121	as it is written, "by the hand of the prophets I use similitudes." So these images
122	and these revelations are called contractions, and they are called enclothings.
123	But without these enclothings it is impossible to grasp HaShem at all; without
124	the enclothings it is impossible, only through garments. And therefore
125	the whole Kabbalah is based on this: that all the worlds, sefirot and partzufim and so on
126	are really garments and clothing for the supernal lights, so that
127	the lower ones will be able to receive these lights, will be able to receive them at all.
128	Okay?
129	So the Rebbe writes here: Divine perceptions can only be attained through
130	many contractions, from cause to effect, from a higher intellect to a lower intellect.
131	According to what will be explained further in this Torah, higher intellect means Chochmah,
132	and lower intellect is Malchut.
133	In the secret of the sefirot, yes, it is written: "How many are Your works, HaShem,
134	You made them all in wisdom."
135	Our Rabbis the Kabbalists write that...
136	the word "asita" (You made) comes from "asiyah" (making), and asiyah is like the world of Asiyah, which corresponds to the sefirah of Malchut.
137	And the light of Chochmah is enclothed in Malchut, and through this
138	it is revealed in the lower worlds.
139	And so Rabbi Nachman also writes in the first Torah in Likutei Moharan, called Torat Ayelet Chen.
140	And therefore it is written, "How many are Your works, HaShem, You made them all in wisdom."
141	The moment you say the words "wisdom" and "You made," it is the enclothing of Chochmah in Malchut.
142	Understood?
143	And here in this Torah we will see that by higher intellect, the Rebbe means
144	Chochmah, and by lower intellect, Malchut.
145	The Rebbe writes here, as we see with our senses, that one cannot grasp a great
146	intellect except through its enclothing in the lower intellect.
147	Meaning of the words.
148	I want to give a parable, my friends, and illustrate the matter so that it will be understood.
149	The Rebbe says here, "as we see with our senses."
150	When the Rebbe says "as we see with our senses," and these are also the expressions of the Arizal,
151	"as we see with our senses," or "as we see with the eyes," and so on, they mean,
152	my friends, that you should look at our world,
153	at concepts that you know, and you will understand what I want to tell you.
154	So I will give you an example.
155	Suppose there is a great rabbi, a great teacher, who is now teaching his student
156	a certain subject, and he sees that the student has difficulty understanding the concepts.
157	So if he is a good teacher, he knows how to teach, in what way to teach,
158	he needs to enter the student's mind, to the concepts the student does know,
159	to examples.
